key_insight: Human and LLM-generated synthesis recipes performed comparably, and their closed-loop collaboration helped uncover a new material, Ba3PtO5, with a previously unreported structural prototype.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that combining AI-generated synthesis planning with expert lab validation can accelerate materials discovery in complex chemical phase spaces.
method: Selected the Ruddlesden-Popper homologous series as a well-studied yet discovery-rich testbed.
Generated synthesis recipes with both humans and LLMs for known and unknown target materials.
Validated recipe success through in-lab experiments and fed results back into subsequent rounds.
evidence_signal: Recipe success was measured experimentally across two rounds, with humans and LLMs showing similar success on known materials and much lower success on unknown materials.
watch_item: Performance dropped substantially on unknown targets, so closed-loop AI guidance still depends on careful experimental verification and domain expertise.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
